passages.original: CAP. III. — Quae igitur apud nos in causa Celidonii episcopi gesta confecta sint, et quae Hilarius dixerit, dum cum eadem, praesente supradicto epi- scopo, audiretur, inditus chartis rerum ordo demonstrat, Ubi postquam Hilarius rationabile quod in sanctorum concilio sacerdotum posset respondere, (j) non habuit, ad ea sc(k) occulta cordis ipsius trans- tulerunt, quæ nullus laicorum dicere, nullus sacerdotum posset audire.
passages.english: CHAP. III. — What, then, was done and settled before us in the case of Bishop Celidonius, and what Hilary said while he was being heard on that same [matter] in the presence of the aforesaid bishop, the order of proceedings set down in the records shows. There, after Hilary had nothing reasonable that he could answer in the council of holy bishops, [his words] passed over to those hidden things of his heart which no layman could say and no bishop could hear.
passages.notes: '(j)', '(k)' are footnote marks. 'sc' read as 'se' (reflexive with 'transtulerunt'); the subject of 'transtulerunt' (plural) is unexpressed, perhaps 'his words' or 'he and his party'; the construction is awkward. 'cum eadem' is unclear; taken as 'on that same [matter]'.

passages.original: Bellum sane quod inter Valen- tinianum imperatorem et Gensericum Vandalorum regem in Africa viguit, litterarum ejusmodi commer- cium impedisse videtur. Viguit autem hoc bellum usque ad an. 442, quo Prosper in Chronico tradit : Cum Genserico autem a Valentiniano Augusto pax confirmata,et certis spatiis Africa idrumque divisa est. Ex novella 23 lib. II moquet an. 443 ex Africains privinciis Valentianiano relictis legatos Romam venisse,et lege fuisse sancitum ut ad præfectum Urbis appellare liceret. Hac forte appellationum occasione quædam apud Mauros illicite usurpata ad S.
passages.english: Certainly the war that raged in Africa between the emperor Valentinian and Genseric, king of the Vandals, seems to have hindered correspondence of this kind. This war lasted until the year 442, in which Prosper records in his Chronicle: "With Genseric, however, peace was confirmed by Valentinian Augustus, and Africa was divided between the two by fixed boundaries." From Novel 23 of Book II we are informed that in the year 443 envoys came to Rome from the African provinces left to Valentinian, and that it was enacted by law that it should be permitted to appeal to the prefect of the City. Perhaps on this occasion of appeals, report of certain things unlawfully usurped among the Moors [reached] the holy
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'idrumque' = 'utrumque', 'moquet' = 'monemur/innotescit' (sense 'we learn'), 'Africains privinciis' = 'Africanis provinciis', 'Valentianiano' = 'Valentiniano'. The sentence continues into the following context ('pontiff ... the account of travellers brought').

passages.original: Et quia evangelica et apostolica fides omnes expugnat errores, et ab uno latere Nestorium dejicit, ab alio Eutychen et participes ejus elidit, hanc regulam mementote servandam, ut quicumque in illa synodo, quae nomen synodi nec habere (d) poterit nec meretur. et in qua malevolentiam suam Dioscorus, (e) imperitiam autem Juvenalis ostendit, dolent, ut dilectionis tuæ relatione comperimus, se metu victos et terrore su- pcratos ad consensum scelestissimi judicii potuisse compelli, et communionem catholicam obtinere de- sideraat, satisfactioni eorum pax fraterna præstetur;
passages.english: And since the evangelical and apostolic faith overcomes all errors, and on one side casts down Nestorius, on the other crushes Eutyches and his partisans, remember that this rule is to be kept: that whoever, in that synod which neither can nor deserves to bear the name of synod, and in which Dioscorus displayed his malice and Juvenal his ignorance, grieve, as we have learned from the report of your Love, that they could be compelled, overcome by fear and overpowered by terror, to consent to that most wicked judgement, and desire to obtain catholic communion, fraternal peace be granted upon their making satisfaction;
passages.notes: '(d)', '(e)' are footnote marks; 'desideraat' read as 'desiderant'. The synod is the 'Robber Synod' of Ephesus (449).

passages.original: Non multo tamen post exarata dicenda est : siquidem Hermes, qui in hac epistola appellatur Archi- diaconus, vivo adhunc Rustico biterrensibus episcopus datus fuit, a quibus cum non fuerit receptus, Narbo- nam rediit, et hac de re idem Rusticus et Hermes litteras ad Leonem dedere, ut ex Hilari paæ epist. 8 colligere licet. His autem ut congruum tempus tribuatur, ante Leonis mortem, quæ contigit an. 461, Her- mes ad Biterrensem cathedram promotus videtur sub an. 460; hæc autem epistola, Hermete adhunc ar- chidiacono Romæ agente, scripta serius dicenda est an.
passages.english: Yet it must be said to have been written not long after: for Hermes, who in this letter is called archdeacon, was given as bishop to the people of Béziers while Rusticus was still alive; and when he was not received by them, he returned to Narbonne, and on this matter the same Rusticus and Hermes sent letters to Leo, as may be gathered from Pope Hilary's Letter 8. To allow a suitable time for these things before Leo's death, which occurred in the year 461, Hermes seems to have been promoted to the see of Béziers around the year 460; and this letter, written while Hermes was still acting as archdeacon at Rome, must be said to have been written at the latest in the year
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: 'adhunc' = 'adhuc', 'biterrensibus' = 'Biterrensibus', 'Hilari paæ' = 'Hilari papae'. The year follows in the next context (459). 'Romae agente' may mean 'acting [as archdeacon] at Rome', though Hermes was archdeacon of Narbonne; the text is as given.
